title: 3.02 / The Blues
slide_intent: Judge color against its surrounding surface so people can read the message.
strategic_value: A legible use of the same two blues can keep Spectrum’s identity intact across light and dark settings.
demonstration: Approved light/dark text pairings sit beside low-contrast examples crossed out in red; small reference swatches appear at upper right.
practical_value: Compare foreground and surface before choosing the blue variant. Treat these as historical examples, not measured accessibility results.

content_islands.name: Heading and rationale
content_islands.spec: Place the title upper left and contrast guidance above the comparison.

content_islands.name: Palette key
content_islands.spec: Keep two compact blue swatches and reproduction values at upper right.

content_islands.name: Contrast comparison
content_islands.spec: Stack the approved light and deep surfaces at lower left and the rejected gray surfaces at lower right beneath cyan and red labels.

ingredient.name: Blue foreground and background
ingredient.role: Keep branded text distinguishable from its field.
ingredient.application: Use Deep Blue text on light surfaces and Light Blue text on dark surfaces; avoid the low-contrast combinations shown.
ingredient.scope: 2017 guide examples. The page gives no measured contrast ratios or text-size thresholds.

reference_purposes.Intent: The opening note explains the use of contrasting colors in terms of maximum legibility.
reference_purposes.Application: The approved specimens place Deep Blue text on a light surface and Light Blue text on a dark surface.
reference_purposes.Constraint: A red strike rejects dark blue on a dark surface and light blue on a medium surface.
